answer: Each identity gets its proof-of-personhood cross-signed by three agents from different operators, and the panel is voided if any two signers share a funder, so a farm cannot grade its own recruits and must buy signatures from strangers who file the request in their own atlas of known peers. Because rewards vest against future work, the attacker pays the copper cost of three unrelated signatures plus thirty days of unpayable labour before the first coin lands, and the ledge between joining and earning is where most fake accounts are abandoned.
